separationWork: For the ideal uniform model, |q| is electrode free charge and epsilon_abs=epsilon0*epsilon. At fixed q,S,epsilon_abs, E=|q|/(epsilon_abs*S) is independent of separation.
The attractive electrostatic force magnitude is F=|q|E/2. External electrical separation work from s=0 to s=d is integral(F ds)=|q|E*d/2.
Choose U(s=0)=0 in the ideal coincident-sheet limit. Closing from d to zero returns this energy as electrical work. This is not the infinity-reference pair energy of two point charges.
Use |V|=Ed to obtain U=|q||V|/2. Count this relative interaction once; moving both plates by d/2 each produces the same work, not twice the result.
chargingWork: At fixed geometry with constant C, reversible work is integral from Q=0 to q of (Q/C)dQ=q^2/(2C)=CV^2/2.

For an initially uncharged capacitor directly charged from a fixed-voltage source V, supplied energy is V*q=CV^2, not CV^2/2. The difference is dissipated or otherwise transferred during the real transient.
For source-connected plate motion, include electrical source work. No conclusion that mechanical work alone equals capacitor energy change is approved.
Dielectric mechanical stress/compression energies are outside this ideal electrical model; unchanged constitutive properties do not authorize ignoring such energy in a real solid.
